A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cwFedAvg and Weight Distribution Regularizer (WDR) research, despite the changed title and extensive revision. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and AG News, alongside scalability, heterogeneity, WDR and personalization analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, including Tiny ImageNet, a synthetic pathway experiment, layer-selection ablations and convergence analyses. Additional empirical results appear in its appendices.

M1.justification: v2 introduces selective aggregation: cwFedAvg operates on upper layers while FedAvg aggregates lower layers. Output-layer-only aggregation becomes the principal evaluated configuration, substantially changing the original full-model procedure. Algorithm 1 also explicitly introduces client-subset sampling. The underlying class-weighting equations and WDR loss remain equivalent.

E1.justification: v2 adds Tiny ImageNet evaluation and a synthetic Gaussian binary-classification task with differently distributed client populations (Section 3.2). MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and AG News remain represented; AG News moves to Appendix D rather than disappearing.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark and scalability comparisons add FedNH and FedUV and remove APPLE. AG News comparisons shrink from seven baselines to FedAvg, FedAMP and FedFomo. The CIFAR-100 personalization heatmaps additionally evaluate FedAMP and IFCA, expanding that particular comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported learning rate from 0.001 to 0.005 and adds ResNet-18 evaluation alongside the CNN experiments. The new synthetic experiment specifies 6,000 samples, three clients and a four-neuron network. The 75/25 split, 1,000-round budget and best-round accuracy metric remain. These reported changes do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds layer-selection ablations (Table 3), average and per-client convergence analyses (Figures 4, 13 and 14), memory scaling analysis (Table 7), and the synthetic pathway case study. WDR and regularization-strength analyses remain, but numerical distribution/WDR ablations cover fewer original conditions, and measured runtime scaling is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three independent runs with different random seeds and use plus/minus entries in accuracy tables. Neither introduces confidence intervals, significance tests or a different uncertainty-reporting procedure. Changes to individual plus/minus values belong to E6.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including Tiny ImageNet accuracies of 41.38 ± 0.12 with the CNN and 43.51 ± 0.14 with ResNet-18, plus layer-selection and convergence findings. AG News cwFedAvg accuracy changes from 98.43 ± 0.04 to 98.19 ± 0.01, with comparator scores and rankings also changing. Pathological MNIST and runtime results disappear. Changed configurations and reported settings prevent a blanket same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: v2 retains the objectives, aggregation mathematics, WDR definition and uniform-class equivalence to FedAvg. Section 4.3 adds the single-class-per-client special case in Equation 9. The explicit normalization derivation and uniform-class proof in v1 Appendices A–B are replaced by abbreviated reasoning, without a new general convergence proof.

C1.justification: The central claims of class-wise personalization, WDR-based distribution estimation and low client communication overhead remain. v2 adds claims that selective upper-layer aggregation reduces server memory while preserving performance, and explicitly claims linear scaling with client count in the conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 develops a class-specific pathway explanation for WDR and motivates selective aggregation through differences between lower- and upper-layer features. It connects convergence behavior to heterogeneity and acknowledges unresolved theoretical relationships beyond output-layer weights. The earlier warning about unstable estimation when classes greatly outnumber local samples disappears; the conclusion instead emphasizes server memory and its mitigation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies CNN kernel sizes, channel counts, pooling and the 512-unit fully connected layer, supplies dataset-specific WDR coefficients, and identifies FastText for AG News. It revises hardware, PyTorch and operating-system details, the repository address and baseline hyperparameter documentation. Some retained-baseline details, including FedFomo's model-download count, are omitted. Newly specified architecture details alone do not establish an underlying architecture change.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around regularization-based PFL through FedNH and FedUV, and around class-dependent weights and critical pathways through works including Kang et al. and Khakzar et al. This literature supports the revised methodological motivation. Several earlier discussions and references on personalization and class imbalance are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. The original separate aggregation and WDR sections become a motivation section followed by a unified algorithm section; personalization analysis is partly moved before the experiments. The appendices are reorganized, terminology is standardized and substantial explanatory prose is rewritten.

P2.justification: The document changes from one column to two columns. The aggregation schematic is redrawn, expanded with FedAvg comparisons and moved to the appendix. New pathway and convergence figures and layer-selection and memory tables are added. Existing heatmaps are rearranged or expanded, and Table 2 replaces runtime columns with communication-cost expressions.

improvement.justification: The layer-selection ablation and memory accounting substantiate a useful practical refinement, while convergence diagnostics, Tiny ImageNet/ResNet-18 evaluation and fuller implementation details strengthen validation. However, removing the previously competitive APPLE baseline and measured runtimes weakens evidence for central comparative performance and efficiency claims. These losses limit the net quality gain.
